## Load packages

`singscore` is called with `::`.

```{r setup}
pacman::p_load(here, dplyr, tibble, purrr, ggplot2, readxl, writexl)
here::i_am("03_Pathway_Enrichment/03_run_singscore/a_script/03_run_singscore.qmd")
```

## Read inputs

singscore (Foroutan et al. 2018, doi:10.1186/s12859-018-2435-4) scores a set within one sample by
its members' mean rank, so a score never sees a contrast and later steps can test it against any
grouping or phenotype. The abundances have the blood index's effect removed.

```{r read}
stage <- here("03_Pathway_Enrichment", "03_run_singscore")
gene_sets <- here("03_Pathway_Enrichment", "00_build_gene_sets", "c_data")
sets <- readRDS(file.path(gene_sets, "gene_sets.rds"))
book <- file.path(gene_sets, "00_build_gene_sets.xlsx")
set_catalog <- read_excel(book, "set_catalog")
protein_map <- read_excel(book, "protein_gene_map")
proteins <- readRDS(here("01_Preprocess", "02_Quantification", "c_data", "proteins_adjusted.rds"))
```

## Score samples

Sets are keyed on gene symbols, so the matrix keeps each symbol's representative protein.

```{r score}
gene_map <- filter(protein_map, selected)
gene_matrix <- proteins$E[gene_map$protein, ]
rownames(gene_matrix) <- gene_map$gene
scored <- singscore::multiScore(singscore::rankGenes(gene_matrix), upSetColc = sets)
scores <- scored$Scores
dim(scores)
```

## Score and dispersion per set

Dispersion, the spread of a set's member ranks, shows whether a score summarises members that
move together.

```{r spread}
set_spread <- set_catalog |>
  filter(qualifies) |>
  select(set_id, database) |>
  mutate(
    score = rowMeans(scores[set_id, ]),
    dispersion = rowMeans(scored$Dispersions[set_id, ])
  )
set_spread |>
  summarise(
    sets = n(), median_score = round(median(score), 4),
    median_dispersion = round(median(dispersion), 1), .by = database
  )
```

## Check participant structure

If participant identity dominates the raw scores, later steps must use within-leg change. The R²
of each leading component on participant measures it.

```{r structure}
components <- prcomp(t(scores))
# proteins$targets rows follow the matrix columns.
tibble(
  component = paste0("PC", 1:4),
  variance_explained = round(summary(components)$importance[2, 1:4], 3),
  participant_share = c(round(map_dbl(1:2, function(i) {
    summary(lm(components$x[, i] ~ proteins$targets$participant))$r.squared
  }), 3), NA, NA)
)
```

## Figure

singscore's `plotDispersion()` draws one signature at a time, so S5 plots every set at once.

```{r figure}
figure <- ggplot(set_spread, aes(score, dispersion, colour = database)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.3, colour = "grey80") +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.4, size = 0.8) +
  scale_colour_brewer(palette = "Dark2", name = NULL) +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size = 3, alpha = 1))) +
  labs(
    x = "mean score across samples", y = "mean dispersion across samples",
    title = "S5. singscore: set score against dispersion"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
  theme(aspect.ratio = 1)
pdf(file.path(stage, "b_reports", "03_run_singscore.pdf"), width = 8.27, height = 11.69)
print(figure)
invisible(dev.off())
```

## Save results

Later steps read `set_scores.rds`: an Excel round trip changes the last bit of some scores, which
breaks singscore's exact rank ties and moves 05's rank tests. The workbook copy is for reading.

```{r write}
saveRDS(scores, file.path(stage, "c_data", "set_scores.rds"))
write_xlsx(
  list(set_scores = rownames_to_column(as.data.frame(scores), "set_id")),
  file.path(stage, "c_data", "03_run_singscore.xlsx")
)
```
